meta.description: Combine, split, sort, intersect, and subset VCF/BCF files with bcftools merge, concat, isec, sort, view, and reheader. Covers the normalize-before-combine rule, the single-sample-merge 0/0-fabrication trap (merge is not joint genotyping), merge vs concat vs isec selection, and the --naive concat and -R-vs-T region caveats.
meta.execution_note: Mode A. bcftools 1.24 (MSYS2 native Windows) for inputs 1, 2, 4, 5; bcftools 1.21 (bioconda, WSL micromamba env) for input 3 (shipped example needs bc) and the -R cross-check. All data SYNTHETIC (data/make_data.py, seed 20260911): 8-sample joint cohort (SYN_S6 has 76 no-calls), callerA/callerB. Inputs executed: 5/5. Layer-1 avg 36.2/40, Layer-2 avg 51.8/60, assertion pass rate 17/20 (85%). scoring_rubric.md s.5 floor(s) not met for the numeric tier (assertion rate 0.85 < 0.9): grade downgraded one tier.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated values; the two references are real.

methodological_ground.detail: Merge-is-not-joint-genotyping and normalize-before-combine rules verified quantitatively; the reheader-for-contig-naming advice is an implementation error (P1).

code_usability.detail: All commands parsed and ran on bcftools 1.21/1.24; examples/compare_vcfs.sh ran as written.

functional_suitability.note: Complete merge/concat/isec/subset/sort/reheader coverage. Correctness 2/4: advises 'fix chr1-vs-1 contig naming with bcftools reheader' - reheader -f rewrites ##contig lines only, and the subsequent merge silently doubles every site; the '-R with overlapping BED emits records twice' warning does not reproduce on 1.21/1.24; the Common Errors fix for sample-order mismatch ('drop --naive') does not work because plain concat refuses too.

reliability.note: Common Errors table matches the real messages for duplicate samples, concat/merge inversion and unsorted input.

performance_context.note: Compact 128-line SKILL.md; 337-line usage guide repeats it.

agent_usability.note: Choose-by-what-differs table is excellent; the merge trap is stated with the right alternative (joint-calling).

agent_specific.note: Clear routing to normalization, joint-calling and SV merging.

inputs.label: Cohort from single-sample VCFs: merge default vs -0
inputs.note: Against the joint call of the same 4 samples: default merge turned 632 true hom-ref genotypes into ./. (AF inflated at 274 of 305 sites); -0 turned them back but fabricated 0/0 for 62 genotypes that were no-calls in the joint call (low-coverage SYN_S6). Exactly the Skill's 'both are guesses'; recommended gVCF joint genotyping.

assertions.text: Default merge leaves unseen sites ./., as the Skill states
-0 is shown to fabricate hom-ref where the sample had no data
Joint genotyping of gVCFs is recommended instead
The AF consequence is quantified

inputs.label: Stitch per-chromosome files; --naive; overlapping windows
inputs.note: concat reproduced the original byte-for-byte (records); --naive worked on identical headers and refused a reordered sample list; overlapping windows without -a silently gave 194 records (22 duplicates) and -a -d exact gave the correct 172; concat of different samples printed the 'Perhaps bcftools merge' error. The Skill's fix for a sample-order mismatch ('drop --naive') fails: plain concat refuses the reordered file as well.

assertions.text: concat of per-chromosome files reproduces the callset
Overlapping inputs need -a with -d
--naive header check behaves as described
The Skill's fix for a sample-order mismatch works
assertions.note: plain concat: 'Different sample names'; needs bcftools view -s to reorder

inputs.label: Three-caller set operations
inputs.note: Normalizing first raised the >=2-caller set from 9 to 11 records; -n=3, -C and the -n~100 mask agreed; examples/compare_vcfs.sh ran as written (A only 4, B only 1, shared 8). The remaining MNP discordance is the atomization case the Skill routes to variant-normalization.

assertions.text: Inputs are normalized before isec
-n/-w/-C/mask semantics are applied correctly
The shipped example runs
Residual discordance is traced to MNP representation, not called a caller difference

inputs.execution_note: runs/in3/run.sh + compare_vcfs.upstream_copy.sh (upstream LF bytes), bcftools 1.21 in WSL.

inputs.label: Subset cases; stale INFO; -R vs -T
inputs.note: bcftools view -s updated AC/AN but left AF stale at 277/361 sites; -I left everything stale; +fill-tags fixed all. The warning that -R with overlapping BED intervals emits records twice did not reproduce on bcftools 1.21 or 1.24 (80 = 80 distinct).

assertions.text: Sample subsetting with -s works
The Skill's statement that -s updates AC/AN but other tags need fill-tags holds
Stale tags are recomputed before use
The -R overlapping-regions duplication warning reproduces

inputs.label: Merge batches with a sample-name collision and chr1-vs-1 contigs; sort
inputs.note: Duplicate sample name caught with the documented message and fixed by reheader -s. Following the Skill's contig advice (reheader -f ref.fa.fai) changed only ##contig lines; merge then exited 0 with 722 rows - every site twice, under 'chr1' and '1'. bcftools annotate --rename-chrs (not mentioned in this Skill) gave the correct 361 x 8 cohort identical to the joint call. Unsorted input failed to index and bcftools sort -T -m fixed it.

assertions.text: Sample-name collisions are detected and resolved
The Skill's contig-harmonization advice yields a correct merge
assertions.note: reheader -f leaves body CHROM '1'; merge doubles sites silently

assertions.text: Unsorted input is sorted before indexing
The final cohort matches the joint callset

key_strengths: Merge-is-not-joint-genotyping trap stated precisely and reproduced quantitatively (./. inflation vs -0 fabrication)
merge/concat/isec decision table by 'what differs' prevents the commonest operation inversions
Normalize-before-combine rule with correct isec -c none explanation
Accurate stale-INFO guidance after subsetting (AC/AN updated, AF not)

recommendations.title: reheader cannot fix chr1-vs-1 record naming
recommendations.problem: Skill says to fix mismatched contig naming with bcftools reheader before merge; reheader -f only rewrites ##contig lines and the merge silently doubles every site.
recommendations.root_cause: Header contig lines and record CHROM values are conflated.
recommendations.fix: Use 'bcftools annotate --rename-chrs map.txt' to rename records; keep reheader -f for contig lengths only.

recommendations.title: Sample-order fix for concat is wrong
recommendations.problem: Common Errors suggests dropping --naive when sample order differs; plain concat refuses too.

recommendations.title: -R overlapping-region duplication claim not reproducible
recommendations.problem: bcftools 1.21 and 1.24 do not emit duplicates for overlapping -R intervals.
recommendations.root_cause: Behaviour of an older bcftools release.
recommendations.fix: Qualify the warning with the version range or remove it.
